scope: Proposition 4.5 (Geometry of the test lattice) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 13-14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The construction in Definition 4.4 gives a finite self-dual lattice L. It is graded of length n + 2, atomistic, coatomistic, and simple. Any two charts 13 intersect in a flat of each, of rank at most m, with the same affine structure on the intersection. Within one chart the primal join of two flats is their affine span if that span has dimension at most n. Attachment preserves all old meets and joins. In particular, flats in two distinct private charts attached at the same W, neither contained in W, have no common proper primal upper bound. There are at least three horizontal comparability components in the interior of L, each containing a chain of distinct comparable interior elements.
